name: Marjapussi
description: Marjapussi is a four-player point-trick game from southern Finland. The name means 'bag of berries' but derives from the French 'mariage' (marriage of King and Queen), reflecting the game's unique mechanic where the trump suit is determined during play by declaring a marriage. Unlike its bidding variant Huutopussi, Marjapussi has no bidding - teams simply score based on points made in play.

overview.description: Marjapussi is a four-player point-trick game from southern Finland. The name means 'bag of berries' but derives from the French 'mariage' (marriage of King and Queen), reflecting the game's unique mechanic where the trump suit is determined during play by declaring a marriage. history.origins: A Finnish game whose name derives from French 'mariage' via the evolution: marias -> marjassi -> marjapussi. The 'bag of berries' meaning is a folk etymology.
timeline: Origins: Derived from marriage games brought to Finland
Evolution: Developed the unique 'declare trumps during play' mechanic
Present: Popular in southern Finland; Huutopussi (bidding variant) is also played
history.cultural: A social game played in Finnish homes and clubs, particularly in the southern regions.
history.evolution: The bidding variant Huutopussi ('bidding bag') was previously described under the Marjapussi name but is now treated separately. This page describes the simpler non-bidding game.

setup.players: 4 players in two fixed partnerships, partners sitting opposite each other.
setup.deck: 36-card pack: A, 10, K, Q, J, 9, 8, 7, 6 in each suit. Can use 32 cards (no 6s) or 28 cards (no 6s or 7s).
setup.dealing: Deal and play clockwise. First dealer chosen at random. Dealer shuffles, player to right cuts. Deal all cards one at a time: 9 each with 36 cards, 8 each with 32 cards, or 7 each with 28 cards. Turn to deal passes left.

rules.objective: Be the first partnership to collect exactly 10 game points. Going over 10 reduces score to 7; losing all tricks reduces score to 0.
rules.gameplay: Player to dealer's left leads to first trick. Must follow suit if able. If no trumps yet, may play any card when void. Once trumps exist, must play trump if void in led suit. Must beat highest card played if able (even partner's card).
keyRules: Follow suit if able; if void in led suit and trumps exist must play trump; must beat highest card in trick if able (even partner's).
Only trick winner may attempt one marriage declaration before leading to next trick; first declaration sets trumps for the hand.
Win by reaching exactly 10 game points; over 10 reduces to 7; no tricks in a hand reduces score to 0.

strategy.basic: Try to win early tricks so you can declare trumps if you have a marriage. The first marriage declaration is crucial as it sets trumps for the whole hand.
strategy.intermediate: Decide whether to declare your own marriage or ask partner. Declaring yourself gives 2 points and sets trumps immediately. Asking partner can be safer but 'breaks' your own marriages. Track which marriages have been 'broken'.
strategy.advanced: The 'half marriage' declaration can be a clever tactic - it breaks all marriages in both hands, preventing opponents from declaring trumps later. Timing when to declare is key: too early and opponents know the trump suit; too late and opponent might declare first.
tips: If you have multiple marriages, you might declare a non-trump one first (if you can win another trick) for the extra game point
The last trick is worth 1 game point - fight for it, especially in close games
If you're at 9 game points, focus on getting exactly 1 more - avoid the 'over 10' penalty
Remember: you must beat your partner's card if you can, even if you'd rather let them win!

variations.name: Tie carryover
variations.description: If card points tie (no game point for majority), that point carries to next deal so taking majority next time scores 2 game points.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Rule change only; no engine constants or deal pattern affected.

variations.name: Ace of clubs leads
variations.description: In the first deal, holder of ace of clubs leads to first trick and becomes second dealer; deal then rotates left as usual.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Lead and dealer rules only; no engine numeric or deal overrides needed.

variations.name: No beat requirement
variations.description: Play without the requirement to beat the highest card in the trick; must still follow suit and trump when void. May be the original rule.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Overtaking rule change; would need trumpConfig override if supported.

variations.name: Lead ace first trick
variations.description: Player who leads to first trick must lead an ace if possible; if no ace, must lead a spade if possible. Later tricks: any card may be led.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Lead restriction for first trick only; no engine path in overrides yet.

variations.name: 32-card pack
variations.description: Use 32 cards (omit 6s); 8 cards each. Same rules otherwise. Requires deckType Standard 32 and rankSet Stripped_32.

overrides.engine.dealPattern: One at a time clockwise; 8 cards each.

variations.name: 28-card pack
variations.description: Use 28 cards (omit 6s and 7s); 7 cards each. Same rules otherwise. Requires deckType Standard 28 and rankSet Stripped_28.

overrides.engine.dealPattern: One at a time clockwise; 7 cards each.

scoring.description: Game points are scored for declaring trumps (2), non-trump marriages (1 each), last trick (1), and majority of card points (1; tie awards none). Card points: Ace 10 or 11, Ten 10, King 4 or 5, Queen 3 or 5, Jack 2 or 5, 9-6 zero (simplified or original system).
scoring.winCondition: First partnership to reach exactly 10 game points wins. Going over 10 reduces score to 7; taking no tricks in a hand reduces partnership score to 0.
